title: Uptight location research: focused follow-up
scope: The initial October 17 pass covers Madison Square, the Clark Avenue Bridge comparison and the possible Leader Drug / Kronheim pairing. Additional dated checks of supplied location claims appear under followUps.
requestStatus: The archive requests below are prepared research leads. No requests have been sent.

cases.status: Probable / high confidence; full facade identification remains open.
cases.searchSummary: Compared the municipal address and previously inspected 1943–1944 and 1955 directories with Hopkins's 1921 atlas, revised in 1924, and a georeferenced historical mosaic. Resolved the building-level address relationship and improved the approximate marker; no complete facade or film camera position was established.

verifiedFacts.text: Plate 6b names MADISON SQUARE BLDG. at the southwest corner of Hough Avenue and East 79th Street, with Hough labels 7812, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 and 7828.

The municipal architects database lists Madison Square Building, 7812–4 Hough Avenue, 1915, demolished, under Albert F. Janowitz. It cautions that not all entries are fully researched; this entry gives no individual permit citation.
The previously inspected 1943–1944 and 1955 directory pages list Madison Square at 7820 Hough Avenue.

inferences: The atlas reconciles 7812–14 and 7820 within one named building frontage. It does not assign numbers to apartment entrances, storefronts or other entrances.
The southwest-corner candidate marker represents an approximate historic building location, not a surveyed boundary, surviving entrance or camera position.
The complete arch, balcony and roofline match in frame 63 remains unproven. Frames 58–62 remain separately unresolved.
cases.negativeResultLimit: The photographs examined in this and the preceding focused pass did not establish a complete facade match. Undigitized photographs, drawings and permits remain outside that result.

cases.searchSummary: Reviewed thumbnails for 61 County Engineer records and selected originals and metadata, 4 Press query results, 12 CPL results (11 photograph records and a subject guide), an approach-view lead and drawing references. County photograph cea0146 provides the new view through the central truss during deck demolition.

verifiedFacts.text: Cleveland Memory cca/129 identifies Michael A. Fuerst's 1984 Clark Avenue Bridge photograph as cea0146, Cuyahoga County Engineer Photography Collection. It looks lengthwise through the central truss after roadway deck removal.

inferences: Frame 658 and cea0146 share compatible haunched frame corners, crossed overhead lattice, a broad rounded far opening, and riveted posts and diagonals. This strengthens Clark relative to the previous low exterior view.
The truss-axis comparison does not reproduce the film's offset camera or intact roadway. Repeated internal frames are not separate bridge spans.

The road edge, railing, complete skyline, furnace equipment and camera position remain unresolved. Frames 653 and 654 need separate equipment comparisons; film-route continuity across cuts is unproven.
negativeResultsAndLimits: The 4 Press results did not add a comparable roadway-axis view; undigitized holdings were outside the check.
The CPL results and credited 1978 approach photograph did not supply an intact central-truss view comparable to frame 658. The approach pony truss is a different structure.
Attempted Library of Congress HAER OH-13 pages were inaccessible. No accessed plan or journal drawing settled the portal geometry. These limits do not establish that suitable sources are absent.

remainingArchiveRequests.target: Cuyahoga County Archives / County Engineer photographs and bridge records
remainingArchiveRequests.request: Seek an in-service view through the former Clark Avenue Bridge's central truss, preferably near 1968. Use cea0146 to compare the intact road edge, railing, internal frame sequence and skyline with frame 658. Ask whether plans or additional photographs establish camera position.

remainingArchiveRequests.target: Cleveland Press photograph holdings and industrial photograph collections
remainingArchiveRequests.request: Seek views connecting the former Clark crossing to furnace and industrial equipment in frames 653 and 654. Assess each film view separately until landmarks establish the connection.

cases.status: Open; Leader Drug branch and furniture pairing remain unplaced.
cases.searchSummary: Reviewed 85 records in the examined CPL directory catalog: the newest Cleveland city volumes located were 1974 and then 1955; no 1968 volume was found there. Inspected the 1974 title leaf and Kronheim and Leader entries. East 55th photograph metadata was located, but attempted original image routes were inaccessible and supplied no visual frontage evidence.

verifiedFacts.text: The verified 1974 directory volume lists Kronheim addresses at 2043 East 55th Street, 15204 Puritas Avenue and 1814 East 40th Street.
The inspected 1974 Leader entry lists 1400 East 9th Street, 5909 Broadway, 11650 Detroit Avenue under Discount, and 17400 Lorain Avenue under Kamm's Plaza.

The 1955 Kronheim lead places retail at 2041 East 55th Street. The Press finding aid separately lists Kronheim Furniture Co. and Leader Drug Stores folders, Subjects series, PH2000.000PRE, printed page 29.

inferences: The 1974 addresses guide further research; they do not establish locations or adjacency during filming in 1968.
These entries are not an exhaustive branch, affiliate or trade-name list. The 1955 number 2041 and 1974 number 2043 do not alone establish an address change, shared storefront or film location.
The partly readable furniture sign may indicate Kronheim. Neither directory entries nor folder names prove a neighboring Leader branch.
cases.negativeResultLimit: No pairing near 1968 was established. Failure to find a 1968 volume in this digital catalog says nothing definitive about other holdings or publication history.

remainingArchiveRequests.target: Cleveland Public Library city, business and street directories
remainingArchiveRequests.request: Request the 1968 Cleveland-proper directory title page, Kronheim and Leader alphabetical entries, classified druggist and furniture lists, and street-address pages for each candidate Kronheim retail address. Start with 2041–2043 East 55th and include both sides of the street and the nearest intersections. If 1968 is unavailable, use 1966 as an earlier control and identify its exact geographic coverage. Seek an addressed advertisement near filming for any Leader affiliate using another trade name.

remainingArchiveRequests.target: Cleveland Press Photograph Collection, PH2000.000PRE, Subjects series
remainingArchiveRequests.request: Check the Kronheim Furniture Co. and Leader Drug Stores subject folders for exterior photographs or contact sheets from 1966–1969. Request the full image and verso or caption, date, address, photographer, and box/folder identifier, prioritizing a view containing both businesses or enough frontage to compare the upper windows, bays and signs with frames 151, 153 and 169. The folder index alone supplies no image-level adjacency.

sources.title: William C. Barrow: Carter Road and Big Four railroad bridge pair, May 23, 2002
sources.note: Cleveland Memory urbanohio/588, gacbridge099.JPG. The caption identifies the Big Four railroad lift in front of Carter Road in this particular broadside view. This clarifies the two structures, not their relative foreground order in every view or their operating status in 1968. Catalog bridge numbering differs from other histories.

sources.title: Bridges of Metropolitan Cleveland: structures across the Cuyahoga River
sources.note: The river inventory lists the Carter-adjacent railroad lift at mile 2.42 and Carter Road highway bridge at 2.43, separately from another railroad lift at 2.24. River-inventory numbers should not be confused with railroad asset numbers.

sources.title: Conrail System Diagram Map, April 1, 1981
sources.note: Original Consolidated Rail Corporation map, AB Number 167. The Ohio list places River Bed Main Line—Cleveland Erie Docks to Literary Street in Category 1, defined by the legend as anticipated line abandonment. The map does not establish a last-train date or daily operation in 1968 and does not substantiate calling the railroad abandoned in the film.

sources.title: Ohio & Erie Canalway: Towpath Trail trailheads
sources.note: Official modern trailhead listings: Scranton Flats, 2057 Scranton Road; Sokolowski’s Overlook, 1203 University Road. These are visitor references, not verified recreations of frame 639 or evidence of a 1968 camera position.

sources.title: Flat Iron Cafe: official address and building history
sources.note: The cafe lists 1114 Center Street and says a late-nineteenth-century fire reduced its former hotel building to two stories. This conflicts with the supplied 1633 West 2nd address and the taller hotel in frame 602. The business history supplies no film-production or temporary HOTEL-sign evidence.

sources.title: Glenn Zahn: B&O Bridge No. 463 under construction, July 3, 1956
sources.note: Cleveland Press photograph, clevbridge015.jpg; Cleveland Memory urbanohio/203. The catalog identifies B&O No. 463 and its jackknife-bascule construction. The 1956 bridge replaced a Scherzer rolling lift; it is distinct from the New York Central / Penn Central vertical lift called Bridge No. 1.

sources.title: William C. Barrow: Baltimore and Ohio Bridge Number 463, May 16, 2002
sources.note: Cleveland Memory urbanohio/413, gacbridge053, Graduate Assistant Collection. The upright long leaf and articulated triangular mechanism provide a probable silhouette comparison for the distant bridge in frame 602. This later opposite-bank view does not identify the hotel or camera point.

sources.title: Jet Lowe: Detroit–Superior east-approach concrete arch, 1978
sources.note: HAER photograph, Library of Congress; Cleveland Memory urbanohio/459. The catalog identifies an east-approach arch. Similar concrete arch construction is therefore insufficient by itself to assign frame 646 to the west approach or a particular street corner.

sources.title: St. Agnes + Our Lady of Fatima: parish history
sources.note: The parish places St. Agnes at East 79th and Euclid, with a 1917 church demolished in 1975. Our Lady of Fatima was established separately on Lexington in 1949. The parishes merged in 1980 and the present adjacent complex was dedicated April 16, 1983. A 1968 film claim must identify a predecessor building; no specific shot has been matched.

sources.title: National Park Service: Cory United Methodist Church
sources.note: Institutional history documents Cory’s civil-rights organizing and community role. It does not establish an appearance in Uptight. The separate municipal landmark record confirms the address at 1117 East 105th Street.

sources.title: Bridges of Metropolitan Cleveland: unusual bridges, chapter 6
sources.note: The chapter gives Clark Avenue Bridge’s total length as 6,687 feet. Its preceding acid-fume/uranium corrosion passage concerns Harvard–Denison, not Clark. The chapter’s 1980 demolition statement must be read at section level alongside County Engineer photographs dated 1984 and 1985; it does not establish the final removal date for the complete crossing.

sources.title: Ohio DOT: IR 490 over Cuyahoga River, 2020 bridge inspection
sources.note: State of Ohio report for Structure File Number 1811991, inspection July 27, 2020. PDF page 2 lists Year Built 1990. This dates the I-490 valley crossing but does not establish that it immediately replaced every Clark Avenue traffic movement.

sources.title: Michael A. Fuerst: Clark Avenue river-span demolition, 1985
sources.note: Cuyahoga County Engineer Photography Collection, cea0824; Cleveland Memory cca/807. The archive dates the river-span demolition photograph to 1985. Together with cea0146 and cea0144 from 1984, it documents staged demolition in 1984–85; no exact final day is inferred from a year-only catalog date.

sources.title: City of Cleveland: Cory United Methodist Church landmark
sources.note: Municipal landmark identity and address: 1117 East 105th Street. This is historical-place context, not a film-production record.

sources.title: Richard Van Curen: United Electric premises at 1830 East 23rd, 1979
sources.note: CSU Office of Campus Planning photograph, Cleveland Memory structure/585. This later industrial facade does not reproduce frame 331’s lighting showroom. It does not establish a 1968 address or corporate continuity with either firm in the 1956 court record.

sources.title: Cuyahoga County: 2019 spring aerial check of proposed Clark pier coordinate
sources.note: The supplied latitude/longitude 41.472714, -81.681121 maps to the center of the inspected 2019 aerial export, on an industrial building roof. This does not substantiate a location for two surviving piers or a film camera. Returned extent, projection and reproducible export URL are recorded in data/research-log.json. Imagery credit: CCFO, CCGIS.

sources.title: Stanley L. McMichael: Clark Avenue crossing dimensions, 1918
sources.note: Contemporary account in Bridges of Cleveland and Cuyahoga County, pages 29 and 32. Clark’s overall 6,687-foot length includes intervening fills; steelwork alone is given as 5,992 feet. These are complete-crossing dimensions, not a single clear span.

followUps.status: Strong visual identification; exact camera position unresolved.

verifiedFacts.fact: The archive identifies the photograph as Carter Road Lift Bridge, looking southeast along its approach, dated July 1986, photographed by Louise Taft Cawood for HAER.

The archive expressly identifies two separate structures: the Big Four railroad lift in the foreground and Carter Road Bridge behind it. It dates the photograph 23 May 2002 and credits William C. Barrow.
verifiedFacts.nomenclatureNote: Its catalog title calls the railroad structure Cleveland, Columbus, Cincinnati, and St. Louis Railroad Bridge Number 5; this differs from the modern No. 2 label found in secondary bridge histories. Preserve the catalog title in citations, but avoid choosing a number for the film caption.

verifiedFacts.title: Conrail System Diagram Map
verifiedFacts.creator: Consolidated Rail Corporation, Office of Chief Engineer, Design & Construction, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
verifiedFacts.fact: The Ohio Category 1 list includes River Bed Main Line—Cleveland Erie Docks to Literary Street. The legend defines Category 1 as anticipated line abandonment.
verifiedFacts.inspection: Original one-page scan and readable list/legend crops visually inspected.
verifiedFacts.limit: This shows an anticipated abandonment in 1981; it does not independently establish the last train date, daily operating status in 1968, or a final 1982 legal abandonment date.

verifiedFacts.title: Bridges of Metropolitan Cleveland: Structures Across the Cuyahoga River
verifiedFacts.fact: The table distinguishes railroad vertical lifts at river miles 2.24 and 2.42; Carter Road highway bridge is listed at mile 2.43. The adjacent pair is therefore the railroad lift at 2.42 and Carter at 2.43.
verifiedFacts.limit: These are river-inventory numbers 8, 9, and 9a, not necessarily railroad asset numbers. Do not apply discussion of the team-track lift at 2.24 to the Carter-adjacent bridge without checking.

inferences: Frame 639’s broad Carter Road tower with a notched crown, narrower adjacent railroad tower and approach-road setting closely match a labeled July 1986 HAER photograph. The comparison identifies Carter Road Lift Bridge with the adjacent Big Four / New York Central railroad lift bridge.

The southeast-facing archive view favors the northwest approach side. The exact film camera position, foreground street and overhead structure remain unverified; the proposed Columbus Road underpass is not established.
limits: The comparison photographs date to 1986 and 2002. A 1981 Conrail map lists anticipated abandonment of the River Bed Main Line; no verified abandonment date or 1968 operating status is assigned here.
The existing point marks the Carter Road bridge landmark; it is not a camera coordinate or a verified place to recreate the shot.
The foreground street and overhead structure have not been independently matched. No continuous geography is inferred from adjacent cuts.

claims.suppliedClaim: Flat Iron Cafe at 1633 West 2nd, with temporary HOTEL sign.
claims.assessment: The Flat Iron Cafe proposal does not fit its official 1114 Center Street address or its published two-story building history. The film’s taller hotel remains unnamed; the HOTEL sign’s production origin is unverified.
claims.positiveFinding: The upright raised leaf and articulated triangular mechanism at left of frame 602 are compatible with the labeled B&O No. 463 jackknife-bascule photographs. This identifies a probable background structure without settling the hotel’s name or camera position.

claims.suppliedClaim: Western Detroit–Superior approach at Mulberry / West Superior, beside Flat Iron Cafe.
claims.assessment: The precise approach arch, river bank and camera position are unverified. The suggested Mulberry Avenue / West Superior Avenue corner is not established, and the current cafe address does not identify it.
claims.positiveFinding: Detroit–Superior strong; Cleveland Union Terminal background viaduct probable.

claims.suppliedClaim: B&O / NS No. 1 river bridge with an exact walkable East Bank viewpoint.
claims.assessment: The proposed B&O / NS No. 1 river-bridge identification does not match frame 667. No steel-company parcel, river-bank camera coordinate or public recreation point is established.
claims.positiveFinding: The matching staircase, ore piles and clamshell bucket identify an ore-handling gantry, without locating its company or parcel.

claims.suppliedClaim: United Electric Supply at 3630 Euclid, since demolished.
claims.assessment: The proposed 3630 Euclid Avenue address and demolition history have not been corroborated. United Electric lettering alone cannot distinguish the similarly named businesses or locate the 1968 shop.

claims.suppliedClaim: Leader Drug at Hough / East 79th, since demolished.
claims.assessment: The proposed Hough Avenue / East 79th Street corner and claimed demolition remain unverified. A period branch record and matching pharmacy/furniture frontage are still needed.

claims.suppliedClaim: Madison Square, with a carved nameplate over its entrance.
claims.assessment: MADISON lettering is visible along the high roofline; the claimed carved nameplate above the entrance is not established at this image resolution. Current survival or redevelopment claims do not strengthen the incomplete full-facade match.
claims.positiveFinding: The named southwest-corner footprint and address reconciliation are retained; full facade identification remains probable.

claims.suppliedClaim: Cory United Methodist Church, 1117 East 105th, as a political-organizing backdrop.
claims.assessment: Address and civil-rights role supported. No specific frame or production record establishes filming at Cory.

claims.suppliedClaim: St. Agnes / Our Lady of Fatima, 6800 Lexington, as a 1968 stone-facade backdrop.
claims.assessment: The present complex was dedicated in 1983. In 1968 St. Agnes at East 79th / Euclid and Our Lady of Fatima on Lexington were separate parishes. An appearance by either predecessor requires a specific frame match.

claims.suppliedClaim: East 79th / Lexington storefront scenes and a continuous Hough route from East 55th to East 79th, with unchanged street grid.
claims.assessment: No specific frame, route log or facade comparison verifies the proposed intersection cluster or continuous route. The separate opening funeral sequence remains cataloged as Atlanta. Current survival and street-condition assertions were not established.

claims.suppliedClaim: Clark roadway looking east into Republic Steel; closed October 16, 1978 because of pollution; removed in the early 1980s; I-490 built shortly after.
claims.assessment: An east-facing camera bearing and the exact Republic Steel furnace alignment remain unverified. Frame 658 does not locate every subsequent industrial cut. The supplied pier coordinate is not a verified bridge-remnant or camera point.
claims.verifiedHistory: McMichael’s 1918 account gives 6,687 feet including fills and 5,992 feet of steelwork. County photographs document demolition in 1984–85. ODOT lists I-490 SFN 1811991 as built in 1990. The exact closure day and Clark-specific corrosion account were not verified in a primary item.

claims.assessment: The supplied point centers on an industrial building roof in the checked spring 2019 county aerial. It is not accepted as a two-pier location or film-camera point. Actual remnant position and current public access remain unresolved.

coordinateCheck.pointMeaning: The supplied point is the exact export center. It falls on an industrial roof in the inspected image.
coordinateCheck.reproduction: x = R * longitude * pi / 180; y = R * ln(tan(pi/4 + latitude*pi/360)). The mean of the returned xmin/xmax and ymin/ymax reproduces this projected point.
coordinateCheck.limit: Aerial imagery is dated 2019. It neither surveys the bridge remnants nor establishes present-day public access or a 1968 shooting position.

followUps.method: Actual film stills, primary archive metadata and selected images, institutional histories and an official county aerial were compared. Negative results are bounded by the records inspected and do not establish that other archive evidence is absent.
